chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Munabbih ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlwān al-Kalbī, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:

I asked the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about the junub and the menstruating woman who perspire in the garment until it clings to them. So he said: “Indeed, menstruation and janabah are where Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has placed them; they are not in the sweat. Therefore, they do not wash their garment.”

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةَ: the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a junub person or a menstruating woman make clothes impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and clothing. It states that the sweat of a person in janabah and of a menstruating woman is not najis, because the state of menstruation and janabah is confined to where Allah has placed it, and therefore the garment touched by their sweat does not need to be washed.
